original.target_description: p. 355 multiple regression with NEO-FFI Openness score as dependent variable and any lifetime substance use disorder as the focal diagnosis predictor, controlling simultaneously for gender and the other two broad diagnosis categories. The full-sample analysis precedes the split-half reliability analyses.

n.sample_role: Participants in the target multiple regression; exact analytic N not stated.
n.exclusions: 490 originally enrolled; 468 assessed at Wave 4. Additional target-regression exclusions/missing-data handling not reported. No diagnostic case count is treated as model N.
n.location: p. 351, Method; p. 355 (PDF p. 6), Analyses Controlling for Comorbidity; compared with pp. 356–357, Tables 3–4 notes
n.quote: Four hundred sixty-eight young adults served as subjects in this study. ... Five regression equations ... were generated using each of the NEO-FFI domain scores as ... dependent variables. The independent variables in each equa- ... tion (entered simultaneously) were gender, any substance use ... disorder, any anxiety disorder, and major depression.

notes: Only unfinished n_o assigned. Target mapping uses the outcome/trait description and p. 355 regression narrative, not row order or numeric matching. Negative emotionality corresponds to the paper's Neuroticism; open-mindedness corresponds to Openness. The p. 355 multiple regressions controlling for gender and diagnostic comorbidity identify the target tests and report beta coefficients and p bounds, but do not state their analytic sample sizes or test-specific exclusions. The Method gives 468 Wave 4 participants. Tables 3–4 explicitly give N = 468 (467 for nicotine dependence), but those notes concern separate hierarchical logistic models, not these target multiple regressions. Cohort N and other-model Ns cannot establish this critical-model analytic N. Candidate only: 468 participants. No arithmetic derivation or group sum used: final cohort groups are not explicitly identified as the complete-case sample for the critical regression.
